actions.description: Share verified situation updates, emerging risks, and resource status with other teams. Free and always available — coordination earns trust.
Switch the regional 911 center to the protected backup circuit and verify end-to-end call routing. Restores 911 reliability while the severed trunk is repaired.
Stand up the backup dispatch center and route emergency calls through it while primary circuits are unstable. Keeps calls from dropping.
Deploy the paper/satellite records fallback at Stillwater and confirm the six dialysis protocols by phone with clinical staff. Patient safety is maintained while the link is down.
Deploy flaggers and temporary signals at the I-81/I-77 interchange and manage approach traffic until the controllers are restored.
Confirm whether the darkened signals are a network outage or a grid fault and report findings so VDOT can focus on traffic, not power.
Call back households on the hotline list, relay accurate status, and point worried callers to the official statement once one exists.
Issue a joint statement confirming the outage is a fiber cut — not an EMP attack — with one verifiable place for updates. Directly counters the rumor.
Deploy a mobile relay unit to Stillwater as temporary bandwidth until the trunk is repaired. Restores telehealth and records access sooner.
Schedule the 15-minute hotwash at the end of the exercise. Every team participates; this is how the simulation improves.
Pull carrier and campus telemetry, correlate the failover against the backhoe strike, and publish a written all-clear (or escalation) that every other team can cite in its own statement.
Move VT Alerts and the research data center to the secondary carrier path and confirm emergency notification actually reaches campus, not just that it was sent.

Contain the hydraulic release before it reaches the storm drain, inspect the shared utility corridor, and release the right-of-way so the fiber splice can begin. Holding it longer than necessary delays every other team.

Switch stores to offline card authorization, verify prescriptions by phone with Carilion clinical staff, and post accurate wait information at the door instead of letting the line invent its own explanation.

Open the state emergency procurement vehicle and underwrite up to $50K of catalog actions that other teams cannot afford this exercise. The state is billed, not the team that acts. Name the recipients and the reason in your report — the money is finite and three teams need it.

Collect status from every team that holds an incident, reconcile it into one regional impact figure plus a yes/no on cyber, and file it before the 9:00 availability. The Governor's office has no independent feed; anything in it that no team verified becomes tomorrow's correction.
